newsitem.title: USA: Burlington Industries sets more spending.
newsitem.headline: Burlington Industries sets more spending.

text.p: Burlington Industries Inc said Thursday it plans to increase capital expenditures to about $135 million in fiscal 1997 from $81 million spent in the year ended September 30.

"This investment will provide for growth and modernization of our U.S. facilities as well as to begin new construction for our Menswear and Denim divisions in Mexico, where we have had operations for more than half a century," chief executive George Henderson told analysts.
He said spending for these purposes are expected to continue near the same level for the 1998-2000 fiscal years.
Henderson said the company is "very optimistic about our growth potential -- both in interior furnishings and apparel fabrics."
"Our apparel fabrics segment has particularly strong growth prospects because sourcing of garments for the U.S. market has shifted closer to home," it said.

He said U.S. garment imports from Asia are declining, and most of the import growth in the future will be in garments made partly in the United States and partly in Mexico or other nearby countries. These garments will consume an increasing amount of fabric made in the Western Hemisphere -- a major benefit to Burlington, which is the largest North American supplier of apparel fabrics, it said.
